“But she’s just a corgi…”  Meet Maple the 4 year old Corgi.  Sweet in the right moments… but dangerous in the wrong ones. Resource guarding food and household items. Multiple bites on owners and family members. Reactive to other dogs on walks, barking & lunging. And now there’s a baby in the home. During the evaluation, Maple tried to bite me multiple times. Not because she’s a “bad dog”… But because she’s been making decisions for a long time without clear direction. No real structure. No consistent boundaries. No clear communication or expectations. And when you let “dogs be dogs” they do just that.  This is the part people struggle with.. You can love your dog deeply and still be missing the leadership they actually need. Honest question… Do you think dogs like Maple know they’re doing something wrong… or are they just doing what’s always worked for them? #DogTraining #dogtrainer #dogsoftiktok #dogs #dog

Beignets from princess and the frog Recipe (made 24) inspiration from Kai 1/2 cups + 1/3 cup whole milk, warm 1/4 cup sugar  1 pack Instant yeast  1 egg ,room temp  2 tsp vanilla extract  2 1/3 cup flour 1 1/4 tsp salt  3 tbsp unsalted butter,softened  Oil Powdered sugar  Honey  1. Activate the yeast In a small bowl, whisk together warm milk, sugar and yeast, 2. Add in melted butter, and egg. stir in flour and salt gradually until a soft dough forms. Knead for 5–6 minutes (by hand or mixer) until smooth and slightly tacky but not sticky. 3. Let it rise Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a towel or plastic wrap, and let rise in a warm spot for 1 to 1½ hours, until doubled in size. 4. Roll and cut Punch down the dough and roll it out on a lightly floured surface to about ¼ inch (0.6 cm) thick. Cut into 2½-inch (6 cm) squares using a sharp knife or pizza cutter. 5. Fry Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Fry beignets 3–4 at a time for 1–2 minutes per side, until golden brown and puffed. Remove and drain on paper towels. 6. Dust & serve Generously dust with powdered sugar while still warm — don’t be shy, it’s part of the charm! Ingredients: ✅ For the Chicken: •2 chicken breast fillets •2 tbsp olive oil Cajun seasoning: •1 tsp paprika (sweet or smoked) •½ tsp garlic powder •½ tsp onion powder •½ tsp oregano •½ tsp thyme •½ tsp black pepper •½ tsp cayenne pepper (to taste) •½ tsp salt ✅ For the Sauce: •1 tbsp butter •1 small onion, diced •1 red bell pepper, diced •250 ml heavy cream •½ tsp bouillon powder (chicken broth) •1 tsp Cajun seasoning •1 handful fresh spinach •50 g Parmesan cheese, grated •50 g Mozzarella cheese, grated •250 g pasta  ✅ For Garnishing: •Chili powder •Fresh parsley 🥩 Preparing & Cooking the Chicken: 1. Rub the chicken breasts with olive oil and generously season with Cajun seasoning. 2. Sear in a pan over medium-high heat for about 2–3 minutes per side until a nice crust forms. 3. Remove the chicken from the pan and place it on a baking sheet. 4. Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (356°F) for about 12–15 minutes, until it reaches an internal temperature of 74°C (165°F). 5. Remove from the oven and let it rest for a few minutes. 🥣 Making the Creamy Cajun Sauce: 1. In the same pan, melt 1 tbsp butter. 2. Sauté the onions & bell pepper until softened. 3. Deglaze with heavy cream and stir in the bouillon powder. 4. Add Cajun seasoning & spinach and let it simmer briefly. 5. Stir in Parmesan & Mozzarella until the sauce becomes creamy. 6. Recipe below  Homemade Cheez-Its Ingredients * 2⅔ cups extra-sharp cheddar cheese, shredded * 1 cup all-purpose flour * ¼ tsp salt * ¼ cup cold butter, diced * 2 tbsp water * Sea salt for sprinkling Instructions 1. Add cheese, flour, and salt to a food processor. Process for 10–15 seconds. 2. Add butter and pulse until crumbly. Add water and pulse until dough starts coming together. 3. Transfer to a bowl and knead briefly until a dough forms. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour. 4. Preheat oven to 375°F. Roll dough out on floured parchment paper and cut into squares. 5. Transfer crackers to a baking sheet, spread evenly, and poke a small hole in the center of each. 6. Sprinkle with sea salt and bake for 12–15 minutes, until puffed and golden. 7. Store in an airtight container for up to 1 week. • • • • • #homemade #recipes #fromscratch #simple #snack

Over-training is one of the most common mistakes I see, so let's talk about that. I usually just train my dogs 5-10 minutes intense work 5-6 days a week, once or twice per day. Not because I can't find time for more, but because I find it much more effective. I like to keep my sessions short, focused, sharp with motivation on top. I want to make sure the dogs are improving. 5-10 minutes doesn't sound like a lot, but I want my dogs to be fully focused the whole session. I train a lot of other things that doesn't require full focus as well (environmental training, impulse control, conditioning etc) but I usually keep my daily obedience sessions short. If I'm training for IGP trial or something that requires longer focus, I'm building the dog a bit different. But my point here is that you don't have to train your dog for hours every day to make it work. It's all in how you train it. This doesn't mean that my dogs are only worked 5-10 minutes per day, of course they get much more exercise. Also, it doesn't mean that you should get a high driven dog just because you can squeeze in 5-10 minutes of training every day. They need more than that!  #DogTraining #dogtrainingtips #dogtrainingadvice #malinois #belgianshepherd #denmark #hundetræning #belgiskhyrdehund #dogsport #dogobedience #obediencetips #obedienceadvice #balanceddogtraining
